name: regtab-rtl
description: RegTab matches tables the way RegEx matches text. RTL (Regular Table Language) is the table-pattern DSL of the RegTab project: syntax highlighting for .rtl files and for RTL embedded in Python and Java string literals, compile diagnostics, live match preview against CSV fixtures, expected-result diffs, and Test Explorer integration.

rtl.fixtures.input.markdownDescription: Template(s) that locate the input CSV table(s) for a `.rtl` pattern. Variables: `${basename}` (pattern file name without extension), `${dir}` (its directory), `${workspaceFolder}`; `${basename/regex/replacement/flags}` applies a snippet-style transform (e.g. `${basename/RtlTask(.+)Test/task_$1/}` maps a host test file to its fixture directory). A trailing `*` glob segment is expanded. Either a single template string, or an array of `{pattern, input}` rules where `pattern` is a glob matched against the pattern file path (first match wins). Examples: `${dir}/${basename}.csv`; `[{"pattern": "solutions/regtab/*.rtl", "input": "${workspaceFolder}/fixtures/${basename}/input_*.csv"}]`.

rtl.fixtures.expected.markdownDescription: Template(s) that locate the expected result CSV(s) to diff the extracted recordset against — symmetric to `#rtl.fixtures.input#`: the same variables and trailing `*` glob, either a single template string or an array of `{pattern, expected, hasHeader?, orderedRows?}` rules (first match wins; the optional booleans override the global comparison settings for that rule). A multi-file expansion pairs with the input expansion positionally (both lists are sorted); a single file applies to every input. An `// expected: path` directive inside the pattern takes precedence (the i-th pairs with the i-th `// fixture:` directive). Patterns with an expected result also appear in the Test Explorer.

rtl.fixtures.expectedHasHeader.description: The first row of an expected CSV holds column names: it is checked positionally against the recordset schema, and only the remaining rows are data.

rtl.fixtures.orderedRows.description: Row order is significant when comparing the recordset with an expected CSV (rows are compared as an unordered multiset otherwise).

rtl.server.path.description: Path to an rtl-lsp executable. Overrides the server bundled with the extension (useful on platforms without a bundled binary).

rtl.trace.server.description: Trace the communication between VS Code and the RTL language server.

scripts.test: npm run check:types && npm run test:grammar && npm run test:unit && npm run check:sync
